claims.text: The as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy has a coarse-grained, inhomogeneous microstructure.
The untreated alloy has limited ductility and localized deformation.
The proposed intervention is room-temperature high-pressure torsion followed by brief inert-atmosphere annealing at approximately 0.5 Tm.
The combined treatment will produce an ultrafine, equiaxed grain structure.
The combined treatment will produce a high density of twin boundaries and dislocations.
High-pressure torsion introduces a high density of dislocations.
High-pressure torsion refines the alloy's grain structure.
Brief annealing relaxes internal stresses.
Brief annealing activates deformation twinning.
Twin boundaries and dislocations provide distributed sites for plastic deformation.
The combined grain refinement, defect structure, stress relaxation, and twinning suppress strain localization.
Suppression of strain localization produces more homogeneous deformation and greater ductility.
Nanoscale grains and retained interfacial features obstruct dislocation motion and thereby maintain high strength.
The treatment preserves energetic interfaces associated with the original chemical composition.
Preservation of the energetic interfaces maintains impact-induced energy release.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by 20–30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will reduce yield strength by less than 5% relative to the as-cast baseline.
Impact-induced energy release will remain statistically unchanged after treatment.
The intervention should be effective for refractory high-entropy alloys with similar compositions and initially coarse microstructures.
Compositions or processing conditions that cause significant phase transformations or grain coarsening fall outside the proposed effective regime.
